steps.title: Prepare all required solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare the reagents listed in the Recipes section, using the exact concentrations, masses, volumes, pH adjustments, filtration, sterilization, and storage conditions as described.

substeps.instruction: 1 M DTT: dissolve 1.5425 g DTT in 8 mL water, bring to 10 mL, filter 0.22 µm, aliquot, store –20 °C in dark.
1 mM Biotin: dissolve 12.2155 mg biotin in 50 mL serum‑free DMEM, vortex, filter 0.22 µm, aliquot, avoid freeze‑thaw.
10× PBS (pH 7.4): dissolve 80 g NaCl, 2 g KCl, 2.4 g Na₂HPO₄·2H₂O, 17.8 g KH₂PO₄ in 800 mL water, adjust pH, bring to 1 L, filter 0.22 µm, store RT or 4 °C.
1 M Tris‑HCl (pH 7.5): dissolve 121.14 g Tris base in 800 mL water, adjust pH with conc. HCl, bring to 1 L, autoclave, store RT.
5 M NaCl: dissolve 292.2 g NaCl in 1 L water, autoclave, store RT.
10 % SDS: dissolve 10 g SDS in 80 mL water, bring to 100 mL, stir (heat if needed), store RT.
100 mM EGTA: dissolve 3.804 g EGTA in 10 mL 1.7 M Tris, add 80 mL water, adjust pH 7.0 with 1.7 M Tris, bring to 100 mL, autoclave, store RT.
1 M MgCl₂·6H₂O: dissolve 20.33 g MgCl₂·6H₂O in 100 mL water, autoclave, store RT (keep closed).
2 M NEM: dissolve 12.513 g NEM in 50 mL isopropanol, aliquot, store –20 °C.

1× Cell Lysis Buffer (CLB): mix 2.5 mL 1 M Tris‑HCl pH 7.5, 1.5 mL 5 M NaCl, 500 µL 1 % Triton X‑100, 500 µL 0.1 % SDS, 500 µL 100 mM EGTA, 75 µL 1 M MgCl₂·6H₂O, 50 µL 250 U/mL Benzonase, 1.25 mL 2 M NEM, protease inhibitor tablet, bring to 50 mL with Milli‑Q water, store –20 °C.

IP Wash Buffer 1: 2.5 mL 1 M Tris‑HCl pH 7.5, 5 mL 5 M NaCl, 500 µL 1 % Triton X‑100, 5 mL 10 % SDS, 500 µL 1 M DTT (10 mM), 500 µL 100 mM EGTA, 1.25 mL 2 M NEM (50 mM), protease inhibitor tablet, bring to 50 mL; add SDS and DTT fresh before use.
IP Wash Buffer 2: same as Buffer 1 but 1.5 mL 5 M NaCl (150 mM) and 0.1 % SDS; add DTT fresh before use.
IP Wash Buffer 3: 2.5 mL 1 M Tris‑HCl pH 7.5, 1.5 mL 5 M NaCl (150 mM), 1.25 mL 2 M NEM (50 mM), protease inhibitor tablet, bring to 50 mL.
10× Running Buffer: dissolve 30.285 g Tris base, 144.4 g Glycine, 10 g SDS in water, bring to 1 L, store RT; dilute 1× before use.
10× Transfer Buffer: dissolve 30.285 g Tris base, 144.4 g Glycine in water, bring to 1 L; before use dilute 1× and add 20 % methanol.
1× PBST: mix 100 mL 10× PBS, 2 mL Tween‑20 (0.2 %), water to 1 L.
Blocking Buffer: dissolve 5 g BSA in 100 mL 1× PBS, store 4 °C.
Antibody Dilution Buffer (streptavidin IB): 0.5 g BSA, 10 mL 1× PBS, 20 µL 0.2 % Tween‑20, 100 µL 0.1 % SDS; add SDS and Tween‑20 fresh.
Blocking/Permeabilization Buffer (IF): 5 g BSA, 300 µL 0.3 % Triton X‑100, PBS to 100 mL, store 4 °C.
Antibody Dilution/Wash Buffer (IF): 15 g BSA, 500 µL 0.1 % Triton X‑100, PBS to 500 mL, store 4 °C.

steps.title: Clone E3‑BirA fusion constructs
steps.instruction: Generate plasmids encoding the candidate E3 ligase fused to BirA at the N‑ or C‑terminus, with and without a GSGS linker, using the BirA vectors listed; also clone the (-2) AP‑Ub construct by inserting the modified acceptor peptide at the Ub N‑terminus.

steps.title: Seed HEK‑293 cells for transfection
steps.instruction: Plate HEK‑293 cells at 1 × 10⁵ cells per well in 2 mL complete DMEM in a 6‑well plate; incubate overnight at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ to reach ~70 % confluency.

steps.title: Transient transfection of constructs
steps.instruction: Transfect each well with the appropriate DNA‑PEI mixture in Opti‑MEM, incubate, and allow expression.

substeps.instruction: Dilute plasmid DNA in 250 µL Opti‑MEM as per Table 1 (e.g., 1.5 µg each of Empty BirA + (-2) AP‑Ub, or BirA‑E3 + (-2) AP‑Ub, etc.).
Dilute PEI in 250 µL Opti‑MEM (~3 µg PEI per µg DNA).
Add PEI to DNA, mix gently, incubate 15–20 min at RT.
Add the 500 µL transfection mix dropwise to the cells.
Incubate 16–24 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Perform proximity biotinylation
steps.instruction: Treat transfected cells with biotin (and optional inducers) using one of two regimes to label proximal proteins.

substeps.instruction: Regime 1: discard transfection medium, add complete medium containing 50–100 µM biotin, add any required inducer, incubate 15 min–6 h (as optimized).
Regime 2: add 50–100 µM biotin directly to the transfection medium, incubate 16 h, discard medium, add fresh complete medium with 50–100 µM biotin and inducer, incubate 15 min–6 h.

steps.title: Harvest cells for lysate preparation
steps.instruction: Collect cells, lyse, and prepare protein extracts for downstream analysis.

substeps.instruction: Wash cells once with 1 mL cold (4 °C) 1× PBS, discard.
Add 500 µL cold 1× PBS, scrape cells, transfer to 1.5 mL tube.
Centrifuge 500 × g, 5 min, 4 °C; discard supernatant.
(Optional) snap‑freeze pellet in liquid N₂ and store –80 °C.
Add 100 µL 1× CLB to pellet, pipette to dissolve.
Sonicate lysate in a 4 °C water bath for 5 min.
Incubate on ice 30 min, pipetting every 10 min.
Centrifuge 14,000 × g, 10 min, 4 °C; transfer supernatant.
Determine protein concentration (BCA assay).
Add 4× Laemmli sample buffer, heat 95 °C for 5–10 min.

steps.title: Run SDS‑PAGE and transfer
steps.instruction: Separate proteins by electrophoresis and transfer to PVDF membrane for immunoblotting.

substeps.instruction: Load 10–20 µg protein per lane on 4 %–20 % Mini‑PROTEAN TGX gel.
Run SDS‑PAGE, then transfer to low‑fluorescence PVDF using standard conditions.
Block membrane in Blocking Buffer for 1 h at RT.

steps.title: Detect biotinylated proteins
steps.instruction: Probe membranes with fluorescent streptavidin and record signal.

substeps.instruction: Incubate membrane with IRdye streptavidin 680 or 800 (1:5,000 in Antibody Dilution Buffer) for 45–60 min in dark.
Wash 3 × 5 min with wash buffer, then 1 × PBS.
Image on Chemidoc MP (fluorescence).
Re‑probe with anti‑HA, anti‑Avi/Ub, and anti‑α‑tubulin antibodies as loading controls.

steps.title: Select optimal construct and conditions
steps.instruction: Compare streptavidin signals across constructs and biotin/inducer regimes; choose the combination giving the strongest specific signal for further experiments.

steps.title: Prepare poly‑D‑lysine coated coverslips
steps.instruction: Coat 22 × 22 mm coverslips with poly‑D‑lysine for confocal imaging.

substeps.instruction: Disinfect coverslips with 70 % ethanol, place in 6‑well plate.
Dilute poly‑D‑lysine to 50 µg/mL in sterile 1× PBS.
Add 1.5 mL per well, incubate RT 1 h.
Remove solution, rinse 3 × 2 mL sterile PBS.
Air‑dry in laminar hood ≥2 h.

steps.title: Seed and transfect cells on coverslips
steps.instruction: Plate HEK‑293 cells on coated coverslips, transfect optimal E3‑BirA construct and (-2) AP‑Ub, and treat with biotin/inducer as optimized.

substeps.instruction: Seed cells to reach ≥70 % confluency next day.
Transfect as described in “Transient transfection of constructs”.
Incubate 16–24 h, then apply biotin (50–100 µM) and any inducer per the chosen regime.
Wash 3 × 500 µL 1× PBS to remove excess biotin.

steps.title: Fix cells
steps.instruction: Fix cells with paraformaldehyde before immunostaining.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL 4 % paraformaldehyde (in PBS) per well, incubate 15–20 min RT.
Discard fixative, wash 3 × 500 µL 1× PBS.

steps.title: Permeabilize and block
steps.instruction: Incubate cells with permeabilization‑blocking buffer for simultaneous permeabilization and blocking.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL Blocking/Permeabilization Buffer per well, incubate 1–3 h RT.

steps.title: Primary antibody staining
steps.instruction: Stain cells with anti‑HA primary antibody (or other primary) to assess transfection.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate buffer, wash once with 1× PBS.
Dilute anti‑HA‑Tag antibody in Antibody Dilution Buffer per manufacturer’s recommendation.
Incubate coverslips overnight at 4 °C in a moist chamber.

steps.title: Secondary and streptavidin staining
steps.instruction: Apply fluorescent streptavidin and secondary antibody to visualize biotinylated proteins and primary antibody signal.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate primary antibody, wash 3 × 500 µL Antibody Dilution Buffer, then 2 × 1× PBS.
Incubate with IRdye 680‑streptavidin (1:200) and Alexa Fluor 488‑anti‑rabbit (1:200) in Antibody Dilution Buffer for 1 h at 37 °C in dark, humidified.
Wash 5 × wash buffer (Recipe 20) then 1 × 1× PBS.

steps.title: Mount coverslips and image
steps.instruction: Mount coverslips with antifade DAPI medium and acquire confocal images.

substeps.instruction: Place a drop of ProLong Diamond with DAPI on a clean microscope slide.
Remove coverslip from well, blot excess liquid, place onto slide, avoid bubbles.
Wipe edges, store slides in dark at RT.
Image using a confocal laser‑scanning microscope with 63× oil immersion objective, keeping acquisition settings constant.

steps.title: Scale‑up transfection for proteomics
steps.instruction: Seed four 10 cm dishes per condition and transfect with optimal construct for large‑scale biotinylation.

substeps.instruction: Day 1: Seed 8 × 10⁵ cells in 10 mL complete DMEM per 10 cm dish; incubate overnight 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.
Day 2: Dilute DNA in 500 µL Opti‑MEM (6 µg each plasmid per dish, Table 2).
Dilute PEI in 500 µL Opti‑MEM (~3 µg PEI per µg DNA).
Incubate DNA‑PEI mix 15–20 min RT, add 1 mL dropwise to each dish.
Incubate 16–24 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Induce labeling for proteomics
steps.instruction: Add biotin and any required inducer to label proteins before harvesting.

substeps.instruction: Remove medium, wash cells with 5 mL 1× PBS.
Add 10 mL complete medium containing 50–100 µM biotin and the appropriate inducer.
Incubate 15 min–6 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Harvest cells for proteomics
steps.instruction: Collect cells, pellet, and store or proceed to lysis.

substeps.instruction: Wash 3 × ice‑cold 1× PBS, add 1.5 mL PBS per plate, scrape cells.
Transfer to 15 mL tube, centrifuge 500 × g, 5 min, 4 °C.
Discard supernatant; either proceed to lysis or snap‑freeze pellet and store –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare proteomics lysates
steps.instruction: Lyse cell pellets in CLB, clarify, and quantify protein.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend pellet in 1 mL 1× CLB.
Sonicate in 4 °C water bath (5 min).
Lyse on ice 30 min, vortex/pipette every 10 min.
Centrifuge 14,000 × g, 10 min, 4 °C; collect supernatant.
Measure protein (BCA); use 1–2 mg (minimum 1 mg) for streptavidin pull‑down; keep 2–5 % as input.

steps.title: Streptavidin bead pull‑down
steps.instruction: Capture biotinylated proteins with streptavidin agarose and wash thoroughly.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 40–60 µL streptavidin‑agarose bead slurry to 1.5 mL tube; wash twice with 500 µL 1× CLB (mix, centrifuge 500 × g 2 min, discard).
Add 500 µL clarified lysate (≥1 mg protein) to beads; incubate ≥2 h at 4 °C on rotating wheel.
Collect flowthrough for analysis.
Resuspend beads in 500 µL IP Wash Buffer 1; wash sequentially:
– Wash 2 × 500 µL IP Wash Buffer 1 (5 min rotation, 500 × g 2 min each).
– Wash 2 × 500 µL IP Wash Buffer 2 (same conditions).
– Wash 2 × 500 µL IP Wash Buffer 3 (same conditions).
Resuspend beads in 50 µL 2× Laemmli buffer, boil 95 °C 15 min.
Centrifuge 16,000 × g 5 min RT, transfer eluate to fresh tube; keep 10 % for IP efficiency check, store remainder –20 °C.

steps.title: Assess pull‑down by SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Run input, IP, flowthrough, and wash fractions on gels to verify biotinylation before mass spectrometry.

substeps.instruction: Load 15–30 µg input per lane; load 10 µL IP eluate per lane.
For first‑time IP, also load 20 µL of each flowthrough/wash mixed with 5 µL 4× loading buffer.
Perform electrophoresis and western blot as described in steps “Run SDS‑PAGE and transfer” and “Detect biotinylated proteins”.

steps.title: Mass spectrometry analysis
steps.instruction: Submit eluates for LC‑MS/MS; use TMT or label‑free quantification, process data with MaxQuant or MSFragger, applying FDR < 0.05 for high‑confidence hits.

description: Validation of protocol This protocol has been used and validated in: • Mukhopadhyay et al. [6]. A ubiquitin-specific, proximity-based labeling approach for the identification of ubiquitin ligase substrates. Sci Adv . Controls that were used to validate the protocol: • Successful biotinylation for BirA-E3 and (-2) AP-Ub expressing cells was checked via immunoblotting (Figures 3A and 4A from [6]). This biotinylation was shown to be ubiquitin-specific, since conjugation-deficient (-2) AP-Ub ΔGG mutant abolished protein biotinylation completely ( Figures 2D , S5C, and 4D from [6]). • MS experiments were conducted in triplicate or quadruplicate per condition, and statistical testing was performed ( Figures 2B , 3C, and 4B from [6]). • Identified substrates via MS were validated via denaturing streptavidin pulldown and immunoblotting. The substrates were efficiently pulled down, and ubiquitylation could be visualized by a size shift to higher molecular weight ( Figures 2D , 3E, and 4D from [6]). The pulldown of ubiquitinated species was furthermore validated by treating pulled-down proteins with deubiquitinase USP2, resulting in loss of the substrates from the IP fraction (Figures S2C, S5D, and S6G from [6]).
